title: Turtle Flip at Low Tide
intro_lines: A green turtle hauls up on the sand at dawn.
Its shell is wide and heavy; tide is turning.

outcomes.text: The turtle thrashes, then stills. You net meat and shell, and save the blood for water.
It catches your boot and drags you into the surf; coral cuts sting and the turtle escapes.

choices.label: Leave it and mark the nest

outcomes.text: You note the nesting site for later; eggs appear next week.
A night tide washes the nest away before you return.

history_note: Pedro Serrano flipped sea turtles onto their backs and drank their blood when no rain fell.

title: Tide Pool Harvest
intro_lines: Low tide exposes a reef flat full of pools.
Crabs and urchins crowd the shallows.

outcomes.text: You fill a basket with crab meat and small fish, but an urchin spine pierces your palm.
Clean haul of shellfish; Tide-Puck sniffs out a pearl in the muck.
You avoid stings and collect a modest but safe catch.
A moray lunges from a crevice and bites your wrist before fleeing.

history_note: Tromelin castaways gathered reef fish, crabs and turtles by line, spear and tide-pool gathering.

title: Line Fishing for Jacks
intro_lines: A school of jacks breaks the surface offshore.
Your hand line is short but the water is calm.

outcomes.text: Three jacks strike in succession; you salt the surplus before it spoils.
A reef shark takes the line and your catch; you retreat with nothing.
A fat jack hits; you haul it in and smoke the fillets over driftwood.
Nothing bites; the crab bait rots in the heat and draws flies.

history_note: Tromelin castaways ate reef fish such as jacks, groupers and triggerfish caught by line and spear.

title: Spearfishing the Reef
intro_lines: Clear water, good visibility on the reef shelf.
Large shadows move below the coral heads.

outcomes.text: You land a big grouper, but later tingling and hot-cold reversal set in.
A smaller snapper; safe eating and a clean kill.
Modest catch, no sickness; Tide-Puck gets a scrap of raw fish.
A moray bites your hand in the crevice; you surface bleeding.

history_note: Big reef predators carry ciguatera toxin; the safe rule is to eat small reef fish.

title: Coconut Climb
intro_lines: A tall palm leans over the camp with ripe nuts.
The trunk is rough but slick with rain.

outcomes.text: You reach the top, drop four coconuts, and drink the water in moderation.
Your foot slips; you fall hard, cracking ribs, and the nuts stay up.
Slow but safe; you lower five nuts and a husk for fibre.
The rope frays on bark and snaps; you catch one nut and bruise your shoulder.

history_note: Coconut water is safe in moderation, but too much acts as a laxative.

title: Flint Knapping on the Cliff
intro_lines: A quartz seam juts from the cliff face.
You need an edge for tools and fire.

outcomes.text: A sharp flake breaks free; you wrap it in hide for a blade.
The stone shatters and a splinter cuts your thumb; bleeding stops slowly.
Controlled strikes yield three usable flakes and a core.
The core splits wrong; you salvage one flake and waste the rest.

history_note: The Tromelin castaways used flint strikers left by the French crew until the stones were worn to nothing.

title: Fibre Rope from Husks
intro_lines: Coconut husks pile up behind camp.
Their fibre is tough and water-resistant.

outcomes.text: You spin a length of rope; it holds a heavy load without snapping.
The fibres snap and tangle; you lose material and patience.
Soaked fibre spins smooth and strong; you coil two good lengths.
Over-soaked pulp rots; you salvage one short length only.

history_note: The Tromelin castaways survived fifteen years by using everything: wreck timber, turtles, terns, reef fish and a single shrub.

title: Tar from Pine Sap
intro_lines: Pine resin beads on a sun-warmed trunk.
Your hull needs sealing before the rains.

choices.label: Collect raw sap and boil it

outcomes.text: You render a pot of tar; it seals the canoe seams tight.
The pot boils over and burns your hands; little tar remains.
Slow work, but you gather clean pitch without burns.
A snake drops from the branch; you flee and lose the pitch.

history_note: Careening crews coated hulls with tar and tallow to seal against teredo worm and weed.

title: Driftwood on the Strand
intro_lines: The storm has littered the beach with timber.
Some pieces still bear iron nails and paint.

outcomes.text: You stack dry planks and drift logs; a nail yields scrap iron.
A heavy log pins your leg; you free yourself but lose the haul.
You find a chest fragment with a map piece and a rusted lock.
Nothing marked; you waste the tide window and the wood rots.

history_note: Pedro Serrano used wreck planks as fuel and shells as rain catchers on his barren cay.

title: Salvage from the Wreck
intro_lines: The driftwood trail leads to a half-sunken hull.
Barnacles crust the timbers; something glints below.

outcomes.text: You surface with iron bars and a relic shard, but a shark circles.
The hold collapses; you escape with splinters and a cut.
You pry loose nails and planks; safe but modest salvage.
A tide surge sweeps you off the hull; you swim back exhausted.

history_note: Tromelin survivors salvaged lead basins, timber and iron from the wreck of L'Utile over fifteen years.

title: Shell Rain Catchers
intro_lines: Rain drums on the camp roof.
Empty shells litter the tide line.

outcomes.text: You collect twelve gallons in shells; water tastes of salt and iron.
A shell cracks and spills; you save little and sleep thirsty.

choices.label: Use a sail and channel to a barrel

outcomes.text: Clean rainwater fills the barrel; you boil it to be safe.
Wind tears the sail; water scatters and you lose the cloth.

history_note: Pedro Serrano used shells as rain catchers, collecting up to twelve gallons of water.

title: Rotten timber gives way
intro_lines: A dead kapok leans over your woodpile, trunk punky with rot.
You swing.
The tree answers with a long, wet groan.

outcomes.text: The crown slams into the mud beside you. Splinters fly; you drag two good logs clear.
A branch catches your thigh. You hack free, bleeding, the wood ruined by damp.
The trunk sighs and stays upright. You back away and leave it.
You walk on. The rotted trunk keeps its silence.
It falls overnight, crashing near camp. The noise draws eyes.

history_note: Selkirk on Juan Fernández cut rotten timber for his huts and was nearly buried by a collapsing trunk (DNB).

title: The beds are picked bare
intro_lines: The tide has been generous for weeks.
Today the shells are gone.
The crab beds look picked clean, only shells remain.

outcomes.text: You find a few small crabs under rubble. Thin pickings.
A coconut crab claws your boot as you reach in.
Nothing left. You lose a day.
The reef still gives. You spear a jack and gather shellfish.
A stingray flares as you step past. The barb takes your ankle.

choices.label: Wait for the beds to recover

outcomes.text: You sit out the tide. Nothing gained, nothing lost.
A tideborn scout watches you from the rocks.

history_note: Overharvested crab beds take months to recover; Serrano watched his shellfish vanish after weeks of constant picking (Frontiers 2019).

title: Rivals on the reef
intro_lines: Another camp's smoke rises on the next cay.
Their nets drip.
They work the same reef you do.

outcomes.text: You argue over the reef. They yield the western channel.
They stand their ground. You retreat with a bruised ego.
A fight breaks out. You take a cut to the shoulder.
You steal two fish and a coil of rope from their rack.
A gull alarms the camp. You run with nothing.
They catch you at the waterline. You trade blows, share the catch.
You drop your line in quieter water and pull up a good jack.
A shark follows your bait to the surface.

history_note: Desperate crews poached each other's fishing grounds; Johnson's pirates fought over the best turtling beaches (Johnson 1724).

title: Tide-Puck digs up a cache
intro_lines: Tide-Puck digs at the base of a breadfruit, snuffling hard.
His nose has found something that is not root or rain.

outcomes.text: He unearths a wax-sealed jar of rum, untouched by rain.
It is only a broken compass and rusted nails.
The cache was booby-trapped; a deadfall snaps on his tail.
He whines and looks back at the hole. You walk on empty-handed.
He keeps digging and finds a rusted knife.

history_note: Dogs kept by castaways learned to locate buried stores; Selkirk's cats found his hidden caches nightly (DNB).

title: The axe splits on a knot
intro_lines: The axe bites deep, then gives a cracked bell note.
The head has split on a hidden knot.

outcomes.text: You lash the head with rope and tar. It will hold a week.
The handle splinters too. You are left with a wedged stump.
A free trader swaps it for two hides and a shell.
They want iron. You give up a bar, keep the axe.
No trader is near. You lose the rest of the day.
The adze is slow but true. You finish the cut.
The edge chips on a root. You lose a hand to a splinter.

history_note: Axes and adzes were the most-repaired gear on stranded crews; rope and tar were always on hand for lashing (Pirate Surgeon's Journal).

title: The stranger from the Wake
intro_lines: A week on, a ragged sailor limps into your outpost.
He says he was on the Wake with you.
He asks for shelter.

outcomes.text: He shares dried fish and a map scrap. At dusk he stands between you and a boar charge.
At dawn your tool chest is empty and his hammock is gone. He took your iron and the flint.
He curses you as he vanishes into the palms. You keep your supplies.
Three shadows come for the gate at dusk. You bar it and they melt back into the dark.

history_note: Castaways lied about who owned what on the beach; Selkirk's rescue ship took a man who had stolen from him (RMG).

title: Storm-washed timber
intro_lines: The storm has thrown ship's timber onto the tideline.
Salvaged oak is worth more than the wood you chop.

choices.label: Haul it in before the tide turns

outcomes.text: You drag a 3-metre spar clear. Good hull timber.
A wave slams you and drags the spar back out. You lose a boot.
The sea claims it again at high tide.
It wedges on the reef. You mark it for tomorrow.
You gather rope, a sail patch and a tin cup.
A shark circles the debris and bumps your legs.

history_note: Tromelin's castaways built their escape boat entirely from storm-washed wreck timbers (Archaeology Mag 2014).

title: Coral cuts on the reef
intro_lines: The reef edge is low at this tide.
Shellfish lie in the pools.
The coral under your boots is sharper than it looks.

outcomes.text: You collect clams and a crab without a scratch.
A coral slice opens your calf. Blood in the water.
The ledge holds abalone and a lobster. Worth the risk.
A stingray flares as you step past. The barb takes your ankle.
A moray snaps at your hand from a crevice.
The pools shrink but expose more shellfish.
The tide turns early. You wade back waist-deep.

history_note: Coral cuts on bare feet infect within hours in warm water; NOAA warns reef injuries draw sharks by blood.

title: Smokehouse Trouble
intro_lines: Fish hang over green wood smoke.
Salt crusted on the racks.
Something watches from the scrub.

outcomes.text: Dry fillets and save the bones.
Smoke blinds you; a boar charges.
They smoke it well, eat half.
They nap; gulls strip the racks.

history_note: In the heat and rain, Pedro Serrano's provisions spoiled within two months; meat had to be dried in the sun to last.

title: Salting the Catch
intro_lines: Crabs piled in the sun.
Salt is running low.
Flies already gather.

outcomes.text: Preserved meat for a week.
Heat spoils half the batch.
Smoked crab, tough but safe.
Fire flares; half burns.

history_note: In the heat and rain, Pedro Serrano's provisions spoiled within two months; meat had to be dried in the sun to last.

title: Drying Hides
intro_lines: Green hides staked to frames.
Wind carries the stink.
Goats watch from the rocks.

outcomes.text: Good leather, fewer maggots.
Hide tears; waste of effort.
Supple, water-resistant leather.
Tar smokes; crew coughs.

history_note: Selkirk wore goatskin clothes after tanning hides on Juan Fernández.

title: Stranger at the Kiln
intro_lines: A stranger warms by your kiln.
Hands empty, eyes sharp.
He asks for shelter.

outcomes.text: He repays with a map fragment.
He steals stores at dawn.
He leaves, muttering curses.
He returns with free pirates.

history_note: Serrano's second castaway quarrelled, then reconciled on the cay.

title: Rain Catchment
intro_lines: Rain hammers the canvas.
Shells and leaves wait.
Water runs off the rocks.

outcomes.text: Clean water fills the basins.
Wind tears the rigging.
Brackish lens, drinkable.
Sand collapses; soaked and cold.

history_note: Serrano used shells as rain catchers holding up to twelve gallons.

title: Digging the Well
intro_lines: Sand bites at blistered hands.
Water seeps, then stops.
The tide whispers below.

outcomes.text: Fresh lens found at last.
Collapse buries the tools.
Stable well, steady water.
Stones slip; back strain.

history_note: Tromelin castaways dug a well and walked 750 metres for water.

title: Kiln Firing
intro_lines: Clay pots crack in the heat.
Smoke stings the eyes.
A potter's wheel wobbles.

outcomes.text: Fine pots, few cracks.
Underfired; crumble apart.
Vitrified, strong vessels.
Pots explode; shrapnel cuts.

history_note: Tromelin castaways kept one fire alive fifteen years with wreck timber.

title: Rope Walk
intro_lines: Fibre laid out in long strands.
Hands blister and bleed.
A rat gnaws the hanks.

outcomes.text: Stout rope for rigging.
Weak lay; frays under load.
Rat gone; clean rope.
Puck chews the fibre.

history_note: Rats gnawed Alexander Selkirk's feet as he slept until he tamed feral cats to keep them off.

title: Trading Surplus
intro_lines: A haven boat rides the swell.
Goods laid on a plank table.
Quartermaster counts coin.

outcomes.text: Fair deal, both sides smile.
Short weight; feel cheated.
They pay in gold coins.
They sail off insulted.

history_note: Île Sainte-Marie traders sold cattle to careening crews for guns and iron.

title: Crew Laziness
intro_lines: Noon sun; tools lie idle.
Rum smell drifts from shade.
Work waits undone.

outcomes.text: They work, grumbling hard.
A fistfight breaks out.
Morale lifts; task done.
They drink; nothing done.

history_note: Roberts' articles set lights out at eight and equal liquor shares.

title: Theft from Stores
intro_lines: Storehouse lock is broken.
Footprints lead to scrub.
Tide-Puck growls low.

outcomes.text: Thief caught; goods returned.
Thief escapes; dog tired.
Trap springs; thief yelps.
Nothing but a crab.

history_note: Roberts' articles marooned thieves who defrauded the company.
